title: The $18.7 Million Maple Syrup Heist
sources: BBC News / The Atlantic / Guinness World Records: The Great Canadian Maple Syrup Heist (2011-2012) in Saint-Louis-de-Blandford, Quebec; ~3,000 tons of syrup valued at C$18.7 million stolen from the Federation of Quebec Maple Syrup Producers Strategic Reserve

CBC News / Supreme Court of Canada: Thieves drained heavy ~600-pound steel barrels over months, refilled them with water, and returned them to stacked shelves; discovered in July 2012 when inspector Michel Gauvreau climbed a stack and noticed a nearly empty, rusting barrel leaking water

lines.text: Thieves pulled off an eighteen million dollar heist in Canada
lines.caps: Thieves | pulled off | an eighteen | million dollar | heist | in Canada

lines.text: by stealing three thousand tons of pure maple syrup.
lines.caps: by stealing | three thousand | tons | of pure | maple syrup.

lines.text: See, Quebec locks away reserve syrup in giant warehouses,
stacked high with thousands of heavy steel barrels.
One night, a sneaky crew slipped past the security,
rolled out six hundred pound barrels one by one,
and drained every last golden drop.
Instead of leaving suspicious empty cans behind,
they filled those exact same barrels up with tap water,
and stacked them neatly right back on the shelves.
Nobody noticed a thing for almost an entire year.
Until an inspector climbed the towering stacks,
nudged a rusty barrel that felt way too light,
and watched clear water pour out onto the floor.
Proving even syrup crooks can wash up empty.
